title: AI-Assisted Project Status and Steering Pack Production (2026)

questions.question: A T4 signal is five days old. Is it admissible under STALENESS_THRESHOLD_DAYS?
options: Yes, because T4 signals remain admissible for up to 14 days
No, because every steering signal must be younger than one day
No, because T4 is qualitative and can never support a pack
Yes, but only if it is also marked as a blocker
questions.explanation: T4 has the widest threshold in the table: 14 days. A five-day-old proxy is therefore admissible, although it cannot by itself support status confirmation without T1/T2 evidence.

questions.question: Why does scenario B, with only admissible T4 signals, route to RISK_ESCALATION?
options: A T4 signal always creates a blocker regardless of its age
The signals are admissible but no T1 or T2 evidence is present to confirm status
The router ignores all T4 signals before checking freshness
RISK_ESCALATION is the default for every healthy project
questions.explanation: The T4 signals pass their 14-day freshness window, but route_section reserves STATUS_CONFIRMATION for admissible T1/T2 evidence. T3/T4-only evidence is routed to escalation and fails the tier-coverage gate.

questions.question: What changes when scenario B gains a fresh T1 API error-rate signal?
options: It becomes DECISION_REQUEST because adding a signal invalidates the old evidence
It stays RISK_ESCALATION because T4 evidence always dominates T1
It becomes STATUS_CONFIRMATION and clears the no-T1/T2 quality gate
It becomes BLOCKED because three signals exceed the pack limit
questions.explanation: The added T1 signal is fresh and admissible. With T1 evidence present and no blocker or threshold breach, route_section selects STATUS_CONFIRMATION and the tier gate passes.

questions.question: What section type has priority in scenario D, where an admissible dependency signal is_blocker=True?
options: STATUS_CONFIRMATION, because the production error rate is fresh
RISK_ESCALATION, because every blocker is only a threshold breach
STATUS_CONFIRMATION, because T1/T2 evidence always outranks blockers
DECISION_REQUEST, because an admissible blocker requires a steering decision
questions.explanation: route_section checks admissible blockers first. The dependency blocker therefore selects DECISION_REQUEST before it considers threshold breaches or evidence tiers.

questions.question: What does scenario C route_section return when fresh T1/T2 evidence exists but a fresh T2 scope signal has threshold_breached=True?
options: RISK_ESCALATION, because a threshold breach outranks ordinary status confirmation
STATUS_CONFIRMATION, because any T1 signal suppresses escalation
DECISION_REQUEST, because stale signals are always blockers
STATUS_CONFIRMATION, because only T4 breaches are actionable
questions.explanation: The stale signals are excluded, but the fresh scope breach remains admissible. A breach is checked before the T1/T2 branch, so the section becomes RISK_ESCALATION.

questions.question: What does route_section return when every supplied signal is stale?
options: STATUS_CONFIRMATION with a note that stale data is acceptable for steering
DECISION_REQUEST plus an evidence-traceability gate failure because no signal is admissible
RISK_ESCALATION with all stale signals treated as current
No section decision; the function raises an exception for an empty admissible list
questions.explanation: When admissible is empty, the router chooses DECISION_REQUEST and adds the zero-admissible-signals quality failure. Stale observations remain visible as rejected evidence rather than being promoted.
